nodes.statement: This is because when the sample size is small, there are some outliers in some simulation runs due to instability of numerical optimization. Numerical optimization becomes more stable as the sample size becomes larger, essentially resolving this issue. When n=100,000, the average F-statistic F_GENIUS =9.48 and GENIUS-MAWII shows negligible bias and nominal coverage, which agrees with our theoretical assessment that GENIUS-MAWII performs well when the identification is not too weak. Across all scenarios, the SEs calculated using are close to Monte Carlo SDs of GENIUS-MAWII. Notice that with m=100 and n=10,000, m^2/n=1 and m^3/n=100 are not small, but the GENIUS-MAWII estimator still performs quite well, indicating that our method is able to work well in typical MR studies with around 100 SNPs and 10,000-500,000 sample size. Under all scenarios, the SEs underestimate the Monte Carlo SDs of the GENIUS-CUE estimator, which is also reflected by the fact that the CPs are below the nominal level 95\%. This is expected because according to our Theorem , a higher order variance term is no longer negligible under many weak moment asymptotics. Comparing the GENIUS-CUE estimator and the GENIUS-MAWII estimator, we see that many weak moment asymptotics indeed provides a better finite sample approximation.

Here, B_1 = O_p(n^-1/2) by finite-dimensional linear model theory. For the second term, using the Strong Schwartz Matrix Inequality, B_2 & = mboxVar (bm Q)^-1 frac1n left\sum_i=1^n R_Y_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T right\ (hatbmmu- bmmu_0) \\ & leq C \| frac1n sum_i=1^n R_Y_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T \| \|hatbmmu- bmmu_0 \| . Similar to the proof of Lemma , we use citet[Theorem 1]tropp2015expected. We calculate the matrix variance parameter v= n^-1 \| E ( R_Y_i^2 (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T bmV_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q) ^T ) \| leq Cn^-1 m . Also note that & left\| (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T right\|^2 = xi_max left\ (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T bmV_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q)^T right\\\ &leq tr left\ (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T bmV_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q)^T right\ leq Cm (bm Q_i - E bm Q) (bm Q_i - E bm Q)^T leq Cm . This implies that L^2 & = n^-2 E \ max_i \| (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T \|^2 R_Y_i^2\ leq C n^-2 m E (max_i R_Yi^2 ) \\ &leq C n^-2 m E (max_i Y_i^2 ) leq C n^-2 m (log n )^2 From the above analysis and Theorem 1 of , we know the matrix variance parameter nu is driving the upper bound and E \| frac1n sum_i=1^n R_Y_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T \|^2 leq C log (m) nu leq C fracm log mn. From Markov inequality, we know that \| frac1n sum_i=1^n R_Y_i (bm Q_i - E bm Q) bmV_i^T \|^2 = O_p( mlog m/n). We showed in the proof of Lemma , \|hatbmmu- bmmu_0 \|= O_p(sqrtmlog m /n). Thus, \|B_2\| = O_p( mlog m/n). The last term B_3 is bounded using the same argument. As the remainder term consists of higher order terms and can be shown to be negligible. Therefore, we have \[ hat omega - omega_0 = O_p(n^-1/2) + O_p( mlog m/n) \] Then, using a similar argument as that for A_2 in Lemma , we have & \| frac1n sum_i=1^n big( bmZ_i-bm D_i bmpi_0 big) bm Q_i^T (hatomega - omega_0) \|\\ &leq \| frac1n sum_i=1^n big( bmZ_i-bm D_i bmpi_0 big) bm Q_i^T \| \|hatomega - omega_0 \| \\ &= O_p(sqrtm log m /n) \ O_p(n^-1/2) + O_p( mlog m/n) \ \\ &= O_p (sqrtmlog m /n ) + O_p ((mlog m/n)^3/2). Thus, we see that part (b) is negligible compared to part (a), so \|hat g(beta_0, hatbm eta) -hat g(beta_0, bm eta_0) \| is asymptotically equivalent with part (a). The proof of (ii) and (iii) are the same as that of Lemma .

Note that by Assumption \ref{assump:omega}, $ n E\{\|\hat g (\beta_0, \bm \eta_0)\|^2 \}/m =  tr(\Omega(\beta_0, \bm \eta_0)) /m \leq C$, so by Markov inequality, $\|\hat g (\beta_0, \bm \eta_0)\|= O_p(\sqrt{m/n})$. Also by Lemma \ref{lemma: g bdd by beta}, Lemma \ref{lemma: g beta, nuisance},  triangle inequality, the compactness of $B$, and $ m^2/n\rightarrow 0 $, 
\begin{align}
   & \sup_{\beta\in B} \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) \|=  \sup_{\beta\in B} \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) -\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) + \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) - \hat g(\beta_0, \bm \eta_0) +\hat g(\beta_0, \bm \eta_0)\|\nonumber\\
    &\leq \sup_{\beta\in B} \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) -\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \|+  \sup_{\beta\in B} \| \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) - \hat g(\beta_0, \bm \eta_0) \|+ \|\hat g(\beta_0, \bm \eta_0)\|\nonumber\\ 
    &= o_p(\sqrt{m}/\sqrt{n}) +  O_p(\mu_n/\sqrt{n})  +  O_p(\sqrt{m}/\sqrt{n})  \nonumber\\ 
  &=  O_p(\mu_n/\sqrt{n}).    \label{eq: g hat bdd in prob}
\end{align}
A useful implication of the above derivation is that $ \|\hat g(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta) \| = O_p(\sqrt{m}/\sqrt{n}) $. 

Let $\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)= \mu_n^{-1} \sqrt{n} \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1}\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) $. By Assumption \ref{assump:omega} and \eqref{eq: g hat bdd in prob}, 
\begin{align*}
    \|\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)\|^2= \mu_n^{-2} n \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1}    \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1}  \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) \leq C \mu_n^{-2} n \| \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)\|^2,
\end{align*}
so that $\sup_{\beta\in B}  \|\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)\|^2 = O_p(1) $. Also, by Assumption \ref{assump:omega} and Lemma \ref{lemma: Omega eta hat}, we have
\begin{align}
    |\xi_{\min}(\hat \Omega(\beta,\hat \bm \eta))-\xi_{\min}( \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)) |\leq \sup_{\beta\in B } \|\hat \Omega(\beta, \hat \bm \eta)- \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \| + o_p(1)= o_p(1), \label{eq: Omega hat bdd}
\end{align}
so that $\xi_{\min}(\hat \Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta))\geq C $ and hence $\xi_{\max}(\hat \Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^{-1})\leq C $ for all $\beta\in B$, w.p.a.1.


Therefore, 
\begin{align*}
  &\mu_n^{-2} n 2 \hat Q(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)= \hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^{-1}\Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta),\\
  &\mu_n^{-2} n 2 \tilde Q(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)= \hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta),
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align*}
    &2\mu_n^{-2} n |\hat Q (\beta, \hat\bm \eta)- \tilde{Q} (\beta, \hat\bm \eta) | \\
    &\leq |\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \{ \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\}\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)| \\
    &\qquad + |\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \{ \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\} \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^{-1} \{ \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\} \hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)  | \\
    &\leq \|\hat a(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)\|^2 \left\{\| \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\| + C\| \hat\Omega(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\|^2 \right\} = o_p(1).
\end{align*}
Consequently, we have shown that 
\begin{align}
    \sup_{\beta\in B} \mu_n^{-2} n |\hat Q (\beta, \hat\bm \eta)- \tilde{Q} (\beta, \hat\bm \eta) | =o_p(1).
\end{align}
Next, we show that 
\[
\sup_{\beta\in B} \mu_n^{-2} n |\tilde Q (\beta, \hat\bm \eta)- \tilde{Q} (\beta, \bm \eta_0) | =o_p(1).
\]
This can be easily seen as  
\begin{align*}
  & 2 \mu_n^{-2} n |\tilde Q (\beta, \hat\bm \eta)- \tilde{Q} (\beta, \bm \eta_0) | \\
  &= \mu_n^{-2}n|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1} \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) ^{-1}\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)| \\
   &=   \mu_n^{-2}n|\{\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)-\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \}^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) ^{-1} \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) +  \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) ^{-1} \{\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\} | \\
   &\leq  \mu_n^{-2}n|\{\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)-\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \}^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1} \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) |+\mu_n^{-2}n | \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) ^{-1} \{\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\} | \\
   &\leq  \mu_n^{-2}n C \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)-\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \| \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) \|+\mu_n^{-2}n C \| \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\| \| \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) - \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \|\\
   &\leq \mu_n^{-2} n  C\sup_{\beta\in B} \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)-\hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \| \sup_{\beta\in B} \|\hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) \| \\
   &\qquad \qquad + \mu_n^{-2} n C\sup_{\beta\in B}\| \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\| \sup_{\beta\in B} \| \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) -\hat  g(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \| \\
   & = o_p(1)
\end{align*}
where the last line is from Lemma \ref{lemma: g beta, nuisance},  $\sup_{\beta\in B}\| \hat g(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\|= O_p(\mu_n/\sqrt{n})$ and $\sup_{\beta\in B}\| \hat g(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)\|= O_p(\mu_n/\sqrt{n})$ from \eqref{eq: g hat bdd in prob}, and $m^2/n\rightarrow 0$. 

Finally, it remains to show that 
\[
\sup_{\beta\in B} \mu_n^{-2} n |\tilde Q (\beta, \bm \eta_0)- {Q} (\beta, \bm \eta_0) | =o_p(1).
\]
For $\beta, \beta'\in B$, let  $Q(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0)= E\{g_i(\beta', \bm \eta_0)^T\} \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1} E\{g_i(\beta', \bm \eta_0)\}/2+ m/(2n) $ and  $a(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0)= \mu_n^{-1} \sqrt{n} \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1} E\{g_i(\beta', \bm \eta_0)\} $. By Assumption \ref{assump:omega} and Lemma \ref{lemma: g bdd by beta}, \\ $\sup_{\beta\in B, \beta'\in B }\|a(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0) \|\leq C $. Then, by Lemma \ref{lemma: Omega multiply},  it follows that 
\begin{align*}
   & \mu_n^{-2}n |Q(\beta', \beta', \bm \eta_0) -  Q(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0)  |= |a(\beta', \beta', \bm \eta_0)^T\{\Omega(\beta', \bm \eta_0) - \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\}  a(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0) | \\
    & \leq C |\beta'-\beta|.
\end{align*}
Also, by triangle inequality, Assumption \ref{assump:omega} and Lemma \ref{lemma: g bdd by beta}, 
\begin{align*}
    &\mu_n^{-2} n |Q(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0) -  Q(\beta, \beta, \bm \eta_0)  | \\
    &\leq C\mu_n^{-2} n \left[\|E\{g_i(\beta',\bm \eta_0) \} -E\{g_i(\beta,\bm \eta_0) \} \| + \|E\{g_i(\beta',\bm \eta_0)\| \|E\{g_i(\beta',\bm \eta_0) \} -E\{g_i(\beta,\bm \eta_0) \} \| \right] \\
    &\leq C|\beta'-\beta|.
\end{align*}
Then by triangle inequality, it follows that $\mu_n^{-2}n |Q(\beta', \bm \eta_0)- Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0)|= \mu_n^{-2}n |Q(\beta', \beta',\bm \eta_0)- Q(\beta, \beta, \bm \eta_0)|\leq C|\beta'-\beta|$. Therefore, $\mu_n^{-2}n Q(\beta,\bm \eta_0) $ is equicontinuous for $\beta,\beta'\in B$. An analogous argument with $\tilde Q(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0)= \hat g(\beta', \bm \eta_0)^T \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1} \hat g(\beta', \bm \eta_0)/2 $ and $\hat a(\beta',\beta, \bm \eta_0) =\mu_n^{-1}\sqrt{n}\Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \hat g(\beta', \bm \eta_0) $ replacing $Q(\beta', \beta, \bm \eta_0)$ and $a(\beta',\beta)$, respectively, implies that \\ $\mu_n^{-2} n |\tilde Q(\beta', \bm \eta_0)- \tilde Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0) | \leq \hat M \|\tilde \beta - \beta\|$ for $\beta,\beta'\in B$, with $\hat M= O_p(1)$, giving stochastic equicontinuity of $\mu_n^{-2} n \tilde Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0)$.

Since $\mu_n^{-2}n Q(\beta,\bm \eta_0) $ and $\mu_n^{-2} n \tilde Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0)$ are stochastically equicontinuous, it suffices by Theorem 2.1 of \cite{Newey1991} to show that 
\[
\mu_n^{-2}n \tilde Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0)= \mu_n^{-2}n  Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0) +o_p(1)
\]
for each $\beta$. Applying Lemma A1 of \cite{Newey:2009aa} with $Y_i=Z_i=g_i(\beta, \bm \eta_0)$, $A= \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1}$, and $a_n=\mu_n^2$. By Assumption \ref{assump:omega}, $\xi_{\max}(A^T A)=\xi_{\max}(A A^T) = \xi_{\max} \{\Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-2} \}\leq C$, $\xi_{\max}(\Sigma_{YY}) = \xi_{\max} \{\Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)\}\leq C$, $E\{(Y_i^TY_i)^2\}/(na_n^2)=$\\ $ E[\{g_i(\beta, \bm \eta_0)^Tg_i(\beta, \bm \eta_0) \}^2 ]/(n\mu_n^4)\rightarrow 0$ from Lemma \ref{lemma: sup g square},   and $n\mu_Y^T\mu_Y/a_n^2\leq C \{ n Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0)/\mu_n^2- m/\mu_n^2\}/\mu_n^2\rightarrow 0 $ from the equicontinuity of $\mu_n^{-2}n Q(\beta, \bm \eta_0) $. Thus, the conditions of Lemma A1 of \cite{Newey:2009aa} are satisfied. Note that $A\Sigma_{YZ}^T = A\Sigma_{ZZ}=  A\Sigma_{YY} = mI_m\mu_n^2$, so by the Lemma A1,

Notice that 
\begin{align*}
	\frac{\partial \Omega(\beta,  \bm \eta_0)^{-1}}{\partial \beta} \big|_{\beta= \beta_0}= - \Omega^{-1}\left[ \frac{\partial \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0)}{\partial \beta}\right] \big|_{\beta=\beta_0}  \Omega^{-1}= - \Omega^{-1} E\big\{ g_i G_i^T + G_i g_i^T\big\} \Omega^{-1}. 
\end{align*}
Recall that $\tilde{Q}(\beta, \hat \bm \eta) = \hat g (\beta, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega (\beta, \bm \eta_0)^{-1} \hat g (\beta, \hat\bm \eta)/2   $, which is the same with $\hat{Q}(\beta, \hat\bm \eta)   $ but with $ \hat \Omega({\beta}, \hat \bm \eta) $ replaced by  $ \Omega(\beta, \bm \eta_0) $. Differentiating $\tilde{Q}(\beta, \hat\bm \eta) $ with respect to $\beta$, we have
\begin{align*}
	\frac{\partial \tilde{Q} (\beta, \hat \bm \eta)}{\partial \beta}  \big|_{\beta= \beta_0} &=\hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega^{-1} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i( \hat\bm \eta)  - \frac{1}{2} \hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega^{-1} E\big\{ g_i G_i^T + G_i g_i^T\big\} \Omega^{-1}  \hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)\\
	&= \hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega^{-1} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta) -  \hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega^{-1} E\big\{  G_i g_i^T\big\} \Omega^{-1}  \hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)\\
	&= \hat{g} (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \Omega^{-1} \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \bigg[ G_i(\hat \bm \eta)- E\big\{  G_i g_i^T\big\} \Omega^{-1}  g_i (\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)\bigg]\\
	&= \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{i, j=1}^n \left\{ G+ \underbrace{G_i(\hat\bm \eta) - G - E(G_i g_i^T) \Omega^{-1} g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)}_{\tilde U_i} \right\}^T \Omega^{-1} g_j (\beta_0, \hat{\bm \eta})\\
	&= G^T \Omega^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta) + \left\{n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n \tilde U_i \right\}^T \Omega^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0, \hat \bm \eta).
\end{align*}
Similarly, we can derive that 
\begin{align*}
&	\frac{\partial \hat{Q} (\beta, \hat \bm \eta)}{\partial \beta}  \big|_{\beta= \beta_0} =  G^T \hat \Omega(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta) + \left\{n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n \check U_i \right\}^T \hat\Omega(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0, \hat \bm \eta),
\end{align*}
where 
\[
\check U_i=  G_i(\hat\bm \eta)- G- \left( n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta)g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \right) \hat\Omega(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^{-1} g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta).
\]
Hence, it suffices to show that\\
(a) $n\mu_n^{-1}( n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n \check U_i- \tilde U_i)^T \hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)=o_p(1)$;\\
(b) $n\mu_n^{-1}( n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n\tilde U_i)^T \{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1}\}\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)=o_p(1)$; \\
(c) $n\mu_n^{-1} G^T \big\{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1} \big\} \hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)=o_p(1) $.

For part (a), we have 
\begin{align*}
     &n\mu_n^{-1}( n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n \check U_i- \tilde U_i)^T \hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\\
     &= n\mu_n^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta) \left\{E(G_ig_i^T) \Omega^{-1}- \left(n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta ) g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \right) \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1}  \right\}^T \hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} \hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta) \\
     &\leq  C \mu_n^{-1} n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2 \left\|E(G_ig_i^T) \Omega^{-1}- \left(n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta ) g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T \right) \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1}  \right \|\\
     &=    C \mu_n^{-1} n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2 \\
     &\qquad \left\|E(G_ig_i^T) \{\Omega^{-1} - \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat \bm \eta)^{-1} \}- \left(n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta ) g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T -E(G_ig_i^T)   \right) \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1}  \right \| \\
     &\leq  C \mu_n^{-1} n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2  \left\|E(G_ig_i^T) \{\Omega^{-1} - \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat \bm \eta)^{-1} \}\right\| \\
     &\qquad+C \mu_n^{-1} n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2  \left\| \left(n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta ) g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T -E(G_ig_i^T)   \right) \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1}  \right \| \\
       &\leq  C \mu_n^{-1} n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2  \left\|  \Omega^{-1}  \{\hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat \bm \eta) - \Omega \}\hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat \bm \eta)^{-1}  \right\| \\
     &\qquad+C \mu_n^{-1} n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2 \left\| \left(n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta ) g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T -E(G_ig_i^T)   \right) \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1}  \right \| \\
        &\leq  C \mu_n^{-1} \underbrace{n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2}_{O_p(m)} \left\{ \left\|   \hat\Omega(\beta_0,\hat \bm \eta) - \Omega  \right\| + \left\| n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n G_i(\hat\bm \eta ) g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta)^T -E(G_ig_i^T)    \right \| \right\}\\
     &=o_p(1)
\end{align*}
 using $ n \|\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\|^2= O_p(m) $ shown in   \eqref{eq: g hat bdd in prob},  $ \xi_{\max} \{ \hat\Omega(\beta_0, \hat \bm \eta)^{-1} \}\leq C  $ shown below \eqref{eq: Omega hat bdd}, $ \xi_{\max} ( \Omega^{-1} )\leq C  $, 
 $\xi_{\max}\{E(G_ig_i^T)\} \leq C  $,  $ \xi_{\max}  \{  E(G_iG_i^T) \}< C,$ and $ \xi_{\max} \{ E(g_ig_i^T)\}\leq C$ from Assumption \ref{assump:omega},   Lemma \ref{lemma: Omega eta hat}(i)-(ii), and  $m/\mu_n^2\leq C$ from Assumption  \ref{assump: many weak moments}. 

For part (b), notice first that from $U_i$ being the residual and Assumption \ref{assump: 4th moment}, we have $E(U_i)=0$ and $E(\|U_i\|^2) \leq E(\|G_i\|^2) \leq Cm  $. From Markov inequality, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{nm}} \| \sum_{i=1}^n U_i \|=  O_p(1)$. Moreover, 
\begin{align}
    &\left\|\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n ( \tilde U_i- U_i) \right\| \label{eq: U_i}\\
    &=  \left\| \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \big\{G_i(\hat\bm \eta) - G_i -  E(G_ig_i^T)\Omega^{-1} (g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta) - g_i) \big\} \right\| \nonumber \\
    &=  \left\| \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \big\{G_i( \hat\bm \eta) - G_i \big\} \right\| +\left\| \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n  E(G_ig_i^T)\Omega^{-1} (g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta) - g_i)  \right\| \nonumber\\
     &\leq  \left\|  \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{i=1}^n \big\{G_i(\hat\bm \eta) - G_i \big\} \right\| + C\sqrt{n} \left\| \hat g_i(\beta_0, \hat\bm \eta) - \hat g(\beta_0,\bm \eta_0)  \right\| \nonumber\\
     &= o_p(1) \nonumber
\end{align}
where the fourth line is because $\xi_{\max}(\Omega^{-1})\leq C$  and $\xi_{\max}\{E(G_ig_i^T)\} \leq C  $, the last line  is from Lemma \ref{lemma: g beta, nuisance}(i)-(ii).   Hence, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{nm} } \|\sum_{i=1}^n \tilde U_i \| =  O_p(1)$. In consequence, by Lemma \ref{lemma: Omega eta hat}(i), and \eqref{eq: g hat bdd in prob},  
\begin{align*}
	&n\mu_n^{-1}( n^{-1} \sum_{i=1}^n\tilde U_i)^T \{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1}\}\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)\\
     &=  \big( \frac{1}{\sqrt{nm}}\sum_{i=1}^n\tilde U_i\big)^T \sqrt{m}\{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1}\} \mu_n^{-1}\sqrt{n}\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta) \\
     &\leq \underbrace{\left\| \frac{1}{\sqrt{nm}}\sum_{i=1}^n\tilde U_i\right\|}_{O_p(1)} \underbrace{\left\| \sqrt{m}\{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1}\} \right\|}_{o_p(1)} \underbrace{\left\| \mu_n^{-1}\sqrt{n}\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta) \right\|}_{O_p(1)}\\
     &= o_p(1).
\end{align*}

Part (c) can be shown in a similar fashion as the Part (b). Specifically,
\begin{align*}
    &n\mu_n^{-1} G^T \big\{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1} \big\} \hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta) \\
    &\leq \underbrace{\|\sqrt{n} \mu_n^{-1} G \|}_{O(1)} \underbrace{\| \sqrt{m}\big\{\hat \Omega(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta)^{-1} - \Omega^{-1} \big\} \|}_{o_p(1) } \underbrace{\| \sqrt{n}m^{-1/2}\hat g(\beta_0,\hat\bm \eta) \|}_{O_p(1)}= o_p(1).
\end{align*}
